name: Hong Kong
title: LGBTQ rights in Hong Kong
extract:
In Hong Kong, lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBTQ) people may face legal challenges and discrimination not experienced by non-LGBTQ residents. LGBTQ rights are generally seen as poor compared to other countries, with a 2025 report concluding LGBTQ people face exclusion "in various domains, including education, economic well-being, family, health, political and civic participation, and personal security and violence."
Public opinion remains divided on the topic. In a 2022 survey, 86% of 18-40 year old respondents agreed that LGBTQ+ people should be treated fairly and should not discriminated against. However, during public consultation of the proposed Registration of Same-sex Partnerships Bill, the government received 10,775 written submissions, in which "around 80%" were in opposition to the proposal.
